I still like the new version !
Same remarks than before:
* Use chess notation for squares
* Give opponent last move

More review! 😆

Title
* Typo?

Rules
* Board & Coordinates

  • Please change "grid" to "board".

  • "The initial board state is provided to your program during the first turn's input.": Only the first player actually receives the initial position, since the second player sees the position after the first move.

  My original suggestion was really to clarify whether every game starts from the standard opening position as described in the official rules, or whether the initial setup can vary. Please revise the sentence to make that explicit instead.

* Movement: Consider mentioning that the Attackers always move first.

* The Throne's Hostility: Please also mention that the Throne is never hostile to the King. Otherwise, the wording can be a bit confusing because "Defenders" refers both to the white side and specifically to the non-King defending pieces.

* Capturing the King: Is the rule for capturing the King adjacent to the Throne intentionally different from the official rules? The illustration under Point 7 of the official rules appears to show the King being captured by only two Attackers even when adjacent to the Throne. If this is an intentional rule change, it should be added to the list of deviations.

* Game End & Score: I originally thought the referee used the score to determine the winner when neither side wins within 200 turns, which is why I suggested documenting how the score is calculated. Since that doesn't appear to be the case, I think all references to score could simply be removed from both the statement and the referee.

Victory Conditions
* Consider swapping the bullet points because throughout the statement the Attackers are usually mentioned before the Defenders.

Output
* (Optional) Since "MOVE" is the only available action, you could simplify the output format to just the four coordinates.

Referee
* Consider revising the exception message "Not your piece" to avoid using "your" in a multiplayer game. It also reads a little awkwardly after "[Player] made an invalid action:".

* Please change the exception message "Move must be orthogonal" to "Move is not orthogonal".

* "Attackers encircled the defenders": Please capitalise "Defenders", and either consistently include or omit "the".

* The exception "Move must not be empty" appears to be unreachable because that case is already caught by "Destination is occupied". Also, a clearer wording would be "Start is the same as destination".

* When an exception occurs, two exception messages are shown in the viewer but none in the console.

* The referee reports different exceptions for "MOVE 1 -1 2 0" and "MOVE 1 9 2 0".

* I've only tested some exception cases so far. I'll do more thorough testing later.

Cover image
* The cover image shows a 8x8 board with more pieces than are used. Consider updating it to better match the actual game. One option would be to use a screenshot of the viewer as the cover image, or as the basis for a new illustration.

Thanks.

Here is Brandubh, an ancient Celtic board game and a fast-paced 7x7 variant of the famous Viking game Hnefatafl! 
I wanted a game with purely asymmetrical gameplay. 

Enjoy! :)

EDIT: Thank to 5DN1L for his first review on a preceeding version of the game!

Once again, incredibly sharp and thorough review! Your feedback was extremely helpful. 
I have synced a new version that addresses (I hope) all the points you brought up:

Rules & Statement:
- Changed "grid" to "board" and clarified that the game always starts from the standard opening position.
- Added that Attackers always move first, and clarified that the Throne is never hostile to the King.
- The rule about capturing the King "adjacent to the Throne" has been removed to match the official rules (the Referee was OK, the statement was wrong!).
- Swapped the victory conditions order and completely removed all references to "Score".

Referee & Code:
- I updated all the exception messages to be more accurate (removed "your", capitalized Defenders, fixed the "orthogonal" message, etc.).
- Fixed the unreachable exception by checking start == end before checking for occupied destinations.
- Brilliant catch on the MOVE 1 -1 bug! :O It was a regex parsing issue (it didn't allow negative signs, which threw a format error instead of an out-of-bounds error). This is now fixed!
- Exception messages are now properly sent to the console.

Output Format: OFC very good suggestion. I completely removed the MOVE keyword from the game. 

Cover Image: I'm still not happy with this one, but it's not my last word! :)

Everything is synced and ready for another look. Thanks again for your amazing help in polishing this game!

Great you're here!
Thanks for the review, I'm on it :)

Updated. 
- Chess notation is now used. To simplify input parsing, I opted to provide the last move in the format `a1b1` rather than `a1 b1`, though both notations are accepted for output. Do you think that’s a good idea ?
It is.  When a capture occurs, x followed by the square coordinates is fine. Of course, no space separator is needed

Thanks for all the praise and the quick update! 

Rules
* Board & Coordinates: Please format "a", "g", "1", "7" and "a1" using the <const> tag instead of enclosing them in backticks.

Input/Output
* Based on the comments, I understand the referee will be updated to accept the input regardless of whether it contains a space. I'll test this once the update is available.

* The statement is now a bit confusing because the opponent's last move is shown without a space, while the output includes one. After the said update is done, consider standardising both formats by omitting the space in both.

* Consider replacing "coordinate" with "square" or "position", which feel more natural when referring to chess notation.

Referee
* The "Destination out of bounds" condition will probably become irrelevant now that input uses chess notation.

* "Attackers encircled the defenders": Please remove "the".

* "Piece does not belong to the current player": Consider simplifying this to "Piece belongs to opponent".

* Please rephrase the message "Only the King can move to the Throne or Corners" to describe the invalid action more directly and use the singular form. For example, "Moves a non-King piece to the Throne or a Corner".

* "The King escaped!" appears in the viewer but not in the console. I suspect the other two messages (encirclement and king capture) have the same issue.

Viewer
* Consider displaying the row and column labels along the edges of the board. Example: https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/mad-knights

* Consider displaying each player's last move below their icon.

* Consider adding tooltips to show each square's position and its occupying piece (if any). You could also add a setting for toggling tooltips, and mention the feature in the statement. Example: https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/flames-extinguisher

* If the board graphics or pieces are derived from someone else's work, please credit the original source. Example: bottom of https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/tower-dereference

Cover image
* I found a source of the current cover image. The previous point on crediting applies here too.

* Personally, I prefer the cover image from the first version, even though it showed the wrong board and pieces. I asked ChatGPT to replace the board while keeping everything else. The result is here: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/151353775dbae8aab6d524acfad6f47ec89782

(Interestingly, ChatGPT titled it "Viking warriors in a mystical game" even though I never mentioned Vikings or Brandubh. I assume it inferred that from either the characters in the image or the board in my prompt.)

I'm not suggesting that you should replace the current cover image, but if you'd like to, you're welcome to use the version I generated (you don't have to credit me 😆), provided the original image wasn't itself created by someone else. If it was, you'd likely need to modify it further or, of course, use a completely different image instead.

Thanks.

Hello, I was already working on most of these points :) Here are the updates:

Rules & Statement:

+ Replaced backticks with <const> tags for all coordinates and values.
+ Standardized the input/output format by omitting the space in the move string (e.g. d2d4).
+ Replaced the word "coordinate" with "square" or "position" to match standard chess terminology.

Referee:

+ The Referee's regex now accepts the input regardless of whether it contains a space or not.
+ Removed the redundant "Destination out of bounds" exception (already caught by regex limits).
+ Removed "the" from the encirclement exception, so it now reads: "Attackers encircled Defenders!"
+ Simplified the exception to "Piece belongs to opponent", and simplified the Throne/Corner rule exception as requested.
+ Victory conditions (King captured, King escaped, Encirclement) are now explicitly logged in the Game Summary console.

Viewer:

+ Added coordinate labels (A-G, 1-7) around the board edges to improve readability.
Integrated the official TooltipModule: hovering over any square now displays its coordinates and the piece occupying it.
+ Added a short end-game cinematic overlay to announce the winner.

Image Credits: Regarding the cover image (and all other game assets like the board and pieces), they were entirely generated using AI generative tools during the development of this puzzle. :) (I can't see the image you created; the link points to this post :) please give me a new link)

Thanks again for the review, everything should be fully synchronized now. :)

This is my 48th build. I can hear my algorithms professor (back in the 90s) shouting at me: "You must ALWAYS save on compilations! Check your code 100 times before submitting it!" :D... Long live 2026 :)
I'm happy to use your image if you prefer, but I can't download it from your "demo" contribution. I'm trying to explain it "calmly" to this dumb AI again. :D

Well, I actually like the pieces in your current cover image! They're better than the generic ones I have (but I got to say the king sitting on the throne in my image is a nice touch 😛). In the end, though, it's really about what *you* prefer rather than what I prefer.

You should be able to download my image easily if you're using Firefox (open Page Info and then go to the Media tab to look for it). But here's the link as well (I'm not sure whether the direct link works): https://static.codingame.com/servlet/fileservlet?id=164476621355316&format=puzzle_cover

Yeah, AI can be pretty dumb. I used a few prompts in order to generate the current one.

What about that one ? :)

EDIT: Well, I still need to fix the number of white & black pieces... but I reached my free quota in generating images for today :D

Yay! That looks awesome! It'll be perfect once the number of pieces is corrected.

If you're using ChatGPT, one thing I've noticed from my experience is that it sometimes messes up the original image if I ask it to edit it within the same chat. I've found it's usually more reliable to start a new chat and ask it to make the edit while keeping everything else unchanged.

We're almost there!

Boss.py3
* Please remove the space in its output format to avoid confusion.

Stub
* Please remove the space between d2 and d4 on lines 5, 12 and 16.

Referee
* Consider displaying a console message when a non-King piece is captured (e.g. [Player] captured the piece(s) at [list of square(s)]).

* The exception "Repeated positions 3 times" appears in the viewer but not in the console.

* Why doesn't the move b3b4 near the end capture the Attacker at c4? https://www.codingame.com/replay/895600175

* Have you verified that the encirclement check works correctly? It's a bit hard for me to test it using hand-drafted moves against the AI boss.

* Likewise, have you verified the "no valid moves" check?

Viewer
* Consider increasing the font size of last moves (e.g. doubling or tripling it).

Cover image
* Number of pieces to be fixed.

Thanks.

Hi! I "think" everything has been addressed in the latest update (fingers crossed):

Boss & Stub:
- Removed the space in the output format in both Boss.py3 and stub.txt

Referee:
- Non-King piece captures are now explicitly logged in the console.
- The "Repeated positions 3 times" exception is now also logged right before the game ends.
- Encirclement Check: I've re-verified the checkEncirclement() logic. It uses a BFS (flood fill) starting from the edges of the board inward. If the BFS cannot reach any Defender or the King, it means they are completely cut off from the edge by attackers.
- No Valid Moves Check: Good catch on this one! :O I found a subtle bug: the check was only looking at immediately adjacent squares (dist=1). If a piece was next to the empty Throne, it thought it couldn't move, failing to realize it could slide through the Throne to the other side. The logic has been rewritten.

Viewer:
- Increased the font size of the "Last Move" text significantly (doubled to 48).

+ I'm still busy on the cover picture though.

Thanks again for the incredible attention to detail! Total mastery :O

EDIT: missed a point: 
Good catch as well for the move b3b4 ! There was indeed a very specific case where the code refused the capture.
If the King was positioned exactly on the Throne (the central square), the Throne's logic took precedence over the King's presence, failing to correctly treat him as an enemy "anvil" for the attackers!! This is fixed as well.

I really appreciate that. 😊 I actually discovered the issue with the move b3b4 by accident, so I'm really glad I caught it before the puzzle's approval!

* At the moment, the console displays the piece capture message before the move message, e.g.
[Player] captured the piece(s) at e4
[Player] played g4f4

Would it read more naturally if these messages are swapped, since the move is what causes the capture?

* The official rules state that the Attackers win if they encircle the King and all his remaining Defenders, whereas the Victory Conditions section only mentions encircling the remaining Defenders. Is this an intentional deviation from the official rules, or does the statement simply need to be updated to match the official rules and the referee implementation?

* The final remaining point is the cover image.

Thanks.

Yes, you're right! Both points have been addressed and pushed:
log ordering fixed & statements updated!

I'm not 100% satisfied with the cover yet, but I think it'll do the trick! :)

Thank you very much :)
